subtitle: After a particular setback, acknowledge what happened, offer a credible repair and let your follow-through carry weight, without pressing people to declare that trust has been restored.
scope: For staff, teams and leaders across DSD and DHS. Original practice cases and private reflection explore credible repair after a setback, not employee trust ratings or individual IDI assessments. Participation in this learning is voluntary. Staff retain their work with guidance, knowledge and feedback available from the Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant. Actual service, information and concern responsibilities remain with their assigned roles. Excluded Native American or Tribal-specific matters go to the appropriate office within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
introTranscript: A setback changes what someone has reason to expect. A missed commitment, an added claim or an ignored contribution can make another promise harder to believe. Rebuilding trust involves more than finding a warm apology: understand the particular effect, make a response that can actually be delivered and notice what follow-through supports. People may remain cautious even when a repair is useful. These examples offer a full practice path, while private understanding is worthwhile without a public story or a demonstrated work change.

lessons.title: Identify the setback before offering reassurance
lessons.summary: Describe a specific missed commitment and its consequence without assigning private motives or declaring the relationship repaired.
lessons.objective: Identify the commitment and observable setback in a practice exchange.
objectives: Identify the commitment and observable setback in a practice exchange.
Distinguish an effect on the work from an assumed intention or private feeling.
Choose an acknowledgment that makes a relevant repair possible.
takeaways: A useful acknowledgment concerns the actual commitment and consequence.
Intent, task performance and private trust are different questions.
Reassurance cannot replace the missing action.
lessons.statement: Start with what happened and what it changed for the other person.

intro.heading: The apology needs an object
intro.body:
In a practice DSD workgroup, Quinn agrees to read Priya’s short comparison before the group chooses which service examples to develop. Quinn does not read it and presents a choice as settled. Priya’s comparison would have raised a different question about the order of the examples. When she points this out, Quinn says that everyone is valued and the group should move forward positively. The statement expresses a general intention but leaves the missed commitment and the decision’s status unclear.

The known setback is specific: an agreed reading did not occur before Quinn presented the choice as settled. Its practical effect is that the group did not examine the supplied comparison in that discussion. This does not establish why Quinn missed it, what Priya privately feels or whether the comparison would have changed the final choice. Keeping those questions separate helps the group respond accurately rather than argue about whether Quinn is a good person.

A useful acknowledgment could be: I said I would read your comparison before that discussion. I did not, and I presented the choice before your question was examined. This names the commitment and consequence without asking Priya to prove an emotional injury or reassure Quinn. It also creates a practical question: who can clarify the actual choice’s status, and what examination remains possible through the appropriate role?

Trust is not the same as cooperation. Someone can keep contributing because the work matters while remaining cautious about a promise. The original organizational trust model by Mayer, Davis and Schoorman distinguishes willingness to accept vulnerability from the actions or outcomes associated with it. Here that concept helps understand a relationship; it is not a reason to rate Priya’s private willingness or record a trust score. Continued work does not prove that the setback had no effect.

A first acknowledgment is not a complete repair. Reading afterward may help, but it does not by itself reopen a choice or give Quinn authority to promise adoption. Naming what happened prepares a response within actual responsibilities. You may privately consider a moment when broad reassurance left an important detail untouched. Use the example if you prefer; no personal confession or colleague account is required.

lessons.keyStatement: A specific acknowledgment lets the next response address a real setback instead of asking general reassurance to do the work.

flashcards.back: An event that changes what someone has reason to expect, such as an unfulfilled commitment or an inaccurate use of their contribution.
A clear account of what you did or did not do and the relevant consequence, without making another person certify your intention.
A response connected with the setback that can be carried out within actual ability, responsibility and authority.
Evidence of an action actually taken after a commitment, kept distinct from a promise or a private feeling.
Continuing hesitation about relying on an arrangement; it is not proof of disloyalty or a failed learning activity.
A statement limited to the evidence available, leaving other experiences and future effects open.

accordion.heading: Name what the reassurance leaves open

items.title: The particular commitment
items.body: Quinn agreed to read a comparison before the discussion. Naming that detail prevents the exchange from becoming a contest over whether everyone is generally valued. The group can examine the reading and missing step without asking anyone for a private trust rating.

items.title: The effect, not a guessed intention
items.body: The comparison’s question was not examined before a choice was presented. Calling Quinn deliberately dismissive or deciding Priya is secretly angry adds information not supplied. Respond to the consequence that is known; any actual concern retains its appropriate process.

items.title: The next decision question
items.body: An acknowledgment can lead to clarification of the choice’s status and who can examine it. It should not promise that Priya’s preferred option will win. Repairing how a contribution is received enables examination; merits and decision authority remain separate.

tabs.label: General reassurance
tabs.body: Quinn says everyone matters but leaves the reading and decision status untouched. Priya would need to raise the practical problem again. The reassurance may express a value, yet it does not identify the action needed for the missed commitment.

tabs.label: A motive verdict
tabs.body: The group decides Quinn intended harm and treats that conclusion as the repair. An unsupported intention claim does not read the comparison or clarify the decision. If a formal concern arises, it belongs with its assigned process rather than a learning discussion’s inference.

tabs.label: A specific acknowledgment
tabs.body: Quinn names the unread comparison and premature presentation. This makes the next question visible without demanding reassurance. It creates a basis for a feasible response while leaving Priya’s private experience and the option’s merits at their proper scope.

check.question: Which statement best begins a relevant repair?
check.correct: Quinn identifies the promised reading, the fact it did not occur and the choice presented before the comparison was examined.
wrong: Quinn explains that everyone is valued, so the comparison no longer needs examination.
The group treats Priya’s continued work as proof that her trust is fully restored.
The group decides Quinn’s private intention without more information and calls that the repair.
check.feedbackCorrect: This names the setback and effect, so the next action can address them without a private trust claim or guaranteed choice.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A general value statement does not supply the missed examination. Cooperation can coexist with caution and cannot prove private trust. A guessed intention does not repair the work or replace a concern process. Begin with the particular commitment and its consequence.

intro.heading: Visible responsibility and private dignity
intro.body:
At a voluntary neighborhood gathering, Rowan promises to bring the short history card Bea prepared for an exhibit. Rowan forgets it. When someone asks why it is missing, Rowan says Bea probably did not finish it. Bea hears this and later says she delivered the card as agreed. Rowan apologizes privately and assumes the matter is closed. Bea points out that the public explanation remains inaccurate.

Bea volunteers that in community theatre work she learned to understand acknowledgment before the group as responsibility for a visible mistake. When an inaccurate public explanation remains, a private apology can leave the other person carrying the reputation cost. For Bea here, correcting the explanation matters more than receiving a long personal apology. Her account does not establish how everyone in theatre or every gathering thinks.

Rowan volunteers that in gatherings with relatives, raising someone’s mistake publicly had often prolonged embarrassment. Rowan learned to understand a quiet acknowledgment as protecting dignity and allowing a person to move on. That familiar meaning made private apology seem like respectful completion. It did not tell Rowan whether the public claim was corrected or what Bea wanted said.

The wider frame holds both purposes: take visible responsibility for the inaccurate explanation and avoid turning Bea into a public emotional performance. Rowan can consider a concise correction to people who heard the claim: I received Bea’s completed card and forgot to bring it; my earlier explanation was inaccurate. This correction concerns Rowan’s action. Bea does not have to tell the gathering how hurt she felt or applaud the repair.

Bea might prefer a different suitable correction or no personal appearance during it. Rowan can hear that choice while retaining responsibility for an inaccurate statement. Understanding a learned meaning does not give either person a permanent communication rule. In actual work, appropriate information responsibilities also remain. Privately, you may recognize why visible accountability or quiet dignity has acquired significance in your own life. That insight matters without naming an identity group or arranging a real apology.

lessons.keyStatement: A changed repair can preserve dignity and visible responsibility when it follows the particular meaning and consequence.

accordion.heading: Trace meaning into a changed response

items.title: Bea’s visible responsibility meaning
items.body: Bea links public acknowledgment with responsibility for a visible mistake. Listeners were told she had not finished the card. Correcting that statement addresses the effect; private apology alone leaves inaccurate information. Her account is useful here without predicting every person’s preference.

items.title: Rowan’s quiet dignity meaning
items.body: Rowan associates privacy with avoiding prolonged embarrassment. That purpose can remain. A concise correction of Rowan’s own inaccurate statement differs from inviting the group to discuss Bea’s feelings. Understanding this difference preserves care while changing the familiar sequence.

items.title: A response that fits both purposes
items.body: Correct the received-and-forgotten card claim without describing Bea’s emotional reaction. Ask about a suitable form where choice matters, and preserve her option not to appear. A correction need not require gratitude or waive actual information responsibilities.

tabs.label: Quiet apology closes everything
tabs.body: Rowan treats private apology as complete because it fits a learned meaning of dignity. The public explanation remains uncorrected. A familiar caring purpose cannot establish that a visible consequence disappeared for Bea or the listeners.

tabs.label: Public emotional performance
tabs.body: The group asks Bea to explain her hurt and forgive Rowan before everyone. This turns visible responsibility into a demand on Bea. Correcting the claim can remain brief and specific without a personal story or declaration of restored trust.

tabs.label: Specific correction with choice
tabs.body: Rowan corrects Rowan’s own explanation and considers a suitable form while preserving Bea’s choice not to participate. Public information can become accurate without private emotion being the price of repair. The personal relationship outcome remains open.

check.question: What follows from the two supplied learned meanings?
check.correct: Rowan can correct the inaccurate public explanation while preserving Bea’s choice about participation and private feelings.
wrong: Everyone who worked in theatre must need a public apology.
Private apology always removes the need to correct a public statement.
Bea must describe hurt and forgive publicly to prove the repair worked.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response changes through actual meaning and consequence, preserving dignity without leaving the inaccurate statement in place.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Bea’s history cannot predict every theatre participant. Rowan’s private sequence does not correct what listeners were told. Public hurt or forgiveness is not owed as proof of success. Address the statement without a group rule or emotional performance.

sorting.heading: Separate learned meanings from a general rule

items.text: Visible acknowledgment can show responsibility for a visible mistake.
The unfinished-card claim remains important here.
Quiet acknowledgment can avoid prolonged embarrassment.
Rowan assumed private apology completed respect.
Every theatre participant needs the same sequence.
Private apology resolves every public consequence.

move.failure: One sequence becomes universal or correction requires public emotion.

lessons.title: Make the next commitment credible
lessons.summary: Connect a repair with actual ability, responsibility and authority rather than make a larger promise to overcome caution.
lessons.objective: Identify what a proposed repair depends on before it is promised.
objectives: Identify what a proposed repair depends on before it is promised.
Distinguish a feasible commitment from an outcome outside the speaker’s control.
Choose a deliverable next action and a relevant follow-up question.
takeaways: A larger promise is not necessarily more credible.
Ability, care and consistency concern the particular task and relationship.
Name what you can do and what needs another responsible role.
lessons.statement: Commit to an action you can carry through, not an outcome you hope will restore confidence.

intro.heading: Do not repair an unkept promise with an unkeepable one
intro.body:
Quinn wants to demonstrate seriousness after missing Priya’s comparison. Quinn promises that her preferred example will become the final choice and that no reading will ever be missed again. The statement sounds strong, but Quinn does not hold final selection authority. Future receiving arrangements involve other roles as well. The promise adds two outcomes Quinn cannot establish.

A credible alternative begins with an action Quinn can perform: read the comparison, preserve its actual question and ask the responsible decision role how it can be examined given the choice’s current status. Quinn can also help arrange a way to confirm examination before presenting a later draft as examined. These commitments matter, but do not guarantee adoption or eliminate every future failure.

The original trust model discusses perceived ability, benevolence and integrity as distinct aspects of trustworthiness. Here these concepts invite questions about the particular repair: can Quinn perform the promised reading, does the response consider the affected contributor rather than seek reassurance, and does the action match the stated commitment? They are not personality diagnoses or employee ratings. Performing the actions also cannot establish that Priya will inevitably regain willingness to rely on Quinn.

Look at the dependencies. Reading is Quinn’s responsibility. Clarifying the choice’s status requires the appropriate role. A future confirmation practice may require the group to agree when material is ready and who confirms examination. Naming a dependency is honest; using it as an excuse to leave an available action undone is different. Quinn can read while the authority question is clarified.

A useful commitment permits a concrete follow-up: was the comparison read, which question was retained and what answer came from the decision role? It should not burden Priya with constantly monitoring Quinn or reporting private confidence. Privately, examine the difference between an impressive promise and a reliable smaller action. The example offers full practice without an employee appraisal or real decision entry.

lessons.keyStatement: A credible commitment connects the needed repair with feasible action and honest dependencies.

items.title: Ability for this task
items.body: Ask whether Quinn can read and summarize this comparison, not whether Quinn is an able person in every setting. Preparation and time matter. A precise action can be checked without a global competence label or a promise about a choice Quinn cannot make.

items.title: Care without reassurance first
items.body: Priya’s contribution needs examination and an honest status answer. Requiring her to say she trusts Quinn before reading reverses the sequence. Care appears in the relevant action; her private account remains hers to offer or withhold.

items.title: Consistency without a guarantee
items.body: Quinn can perform the reading and help agree a later confirmation step. That differs from guaranteeing no failure ever again. Explain the improvement and its limits. If it fails, address the new event rather than treat an earlier promise as proof of current delivery.

tabs.label: Guarantee the preferred result
tabs.body: Promising Priya’s option bypasses examination and exceeds Quinn’s authority. It may look generous while creating an unreliable repair. Making the contribution visible does not mean deciding its merits in advance or compensating for a missed reading with an unsupported result.

tabs.label: Wait for every dependency
tabs.body: Quinn postpones reading because final authority has not replied. An available part of the repair remains undone. Identify the dependency, but carry through the action within Quinn’s control while the appropriate role clarifies what can follow.

tabs.label: Deliver a feasible step
tabs.body: Quinn reads, names the question and seeks a scoped response from the decision role. The next check concerns work performed. This is more credible than a sweeping promise while leaving selection and Priya’s private willingness outside Quinn’s claimed control.

check.question: Which commitment fits Quinn’s actual role?
check.correct: Read the comparison, retain its question and seek an honest response from the decision role without promising selection or restored trust.
wrong: Guarantee adoption even though another role holds selection authority.
Wait to read until every future receiving dependency is resolved.
Require a private trust declaration before reading.
check.feedbackCorrect: The response addresses an available action and names the authority dependency without an invented outcome.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Guaranteeing another role’s choice prejudges the merits and makes the repair unreliable. Waiting for every dependency leaves a feasible step undone. A trust declaration is not the condition for fulfilling a commitment. Choose the reading and a scoped authority question.

items.text: Read and summarize the comparison.
Retain the actual question raised.
Clarify current selection status with its responsible role.
Agree a future receiving confirmation with relevant colleagues.
Guarantee adoption of the preferred option.
Guarantee full private trust.

intro.heading: A cautious response is not disloyalty
intro.body:
In another practice DSD project, Ellis has twice said a draft includes Jo’s comments when the group later discovers two comments were omitted. Ellis acknowledges the omissions and proposes another informal conversation. Jo says she would prefer a list of the actual draft questions and a short response showing which were examined. Ellis hears this as unwillingness to forgive or collaborate.

The example supplies a requested arrangement, not a character conclusion. Jo continues contributing and wants examination to be more visible. A checkable response can reduce ambiguity without requiring reliance on the same assurance that failed. It does not establish that Jo distrusts everyone or has refused all relationships. Actual information responsibilities still determine what belongs in ordinary project material.

Ellis can discuss a workable way to identify the questions and responses rather than collect personal feelings. Making clear which question was examined addresses the request. Requiring forgiveness before discussing the list makes useful work conditional on a private declaration. A person may accept a practical arrangement without offering an emotional account.

Optional repair dialogue is not the only route to a concern response. In a distinct circumstance, a manager receives an allegation that a colleague repeatedly used a protected-class slur. Policy 1436 requires managers and supervisors to immediately report all allegations or incidents of protected-class harassment or discrimination to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. They cannot wait for reconciliation, require a private conversation with the alleged actor or make a finding in this learning exercise. Ordinary draft omissions alone are not automatically a protected-class violation.

Privately, notice whether you interpret another person’s request for clarity as rejection. Understanding your reaction can matter without asking the colleague to relieve it. A suitable response preserves their work and choice, carries actual duties and lets later action supply evidence. Neither a conversation nor this course can require a declaration that caution ended.

lessons.keyStatement: Useful work can continue through a clearer arrangement while the person keeps their private trust account to themselves.

accordion.heading: Receive caution without an added test

items.title: Consider the actual practice
items.body: Jo requests visible questions and responses after omissions. Examine whether this is workable and relevant. Calling her uncollaborative avoids the receiving problem. Necessary work material should not become a feeling log or evidence of an inferred individual orientation.

items.title: Do not demand a declaration
items.body: Forgiveness or renewed trust is not owed to qualify for receiving ordinary work. Ellis can respond without knowing those feelings. A conversation might be offered separately, but declining it cannot become proof of bad faith or grounds for withholding the agreed response.

items.title: Keep the formal duty distinct
items.body: A manager’s protected-class allegation has immediate reporting through its assigned route. Optional repair cannot delay or settle it. Keep both boundaries: do not make an ordinary omission a formal finding, and do not disguise an actual allegation as only a relationship issue.

tabs.label: Clarity as rejection
tabs.body: Ellis reads the requested list as proof Jo cannot cooperate. This supplies a private meaning and leaves the omissions unanswered. Evaluate whether the arrangement helps the actual work rather than infer a character verdict from a request for a check.

tabs.label: Forgiveness as a condition
tabs.body: Ellis offers a list only after Jo confirms forgiveness. The repair now depends on emotional performance. Examine the work response on its merits; a personal conversation remains freely chosen, not the entry price for dependable receiving.

tabs.label: A checkable work response
tabs.body: The group agrees a suitable response identifying which questions were examined. Jo can contribute without discussing feelings. Actual information and concern duties continue, and the clearer arrangement does not establish that every relationship issue disappeared.

check.question: What should Ellis recognize about Jo’s request?
check.correct: A clearer receiving arrangement can support work without requiring forgiveness or proving a private trust state.
wrong: A request for visible responses proves Jo rejects all collaboration.
Jo must forgive Ellis before the group examines a suitable list.
A manager may delay protected-class allegation reporting until a repair discussion ends.
check.feedbackCorrect: This receives the practical request at its scope while preserving choice and separate duties.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A requested check does not prove refusal to collaborate. Forgiveness is not the condition for examining ordinary work. A protected-class allegation retains immediate manager reporting even when dialogue is offered. Receive the arrangement without a private test or delayed formal response.

items.text: Identify draft questions and which were examined.
Use approved material for necessary project responses.
Require forgiveness before considering a list.
Collect trust ratings as the condition for contribution.
A manager immediately reports a protected-class allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer.
Follow agency complaint and investigation procedures.

intro.heading: The promise is not the receipt
intro.body:
Quinn reads Priya’s comparison and accurately summarizes its question about the order of service examples. The responsible role explains that the earlier choice was a draft selection and arranges examination before the next draft. These actions are known. They establish more than a promise, but do not establish adoption of Priya’s preferred option or complete private confidence.

Follow-through concerns the action and what it enabled. Was the comparison read? Did the summary preserve the actual question rather than a more convenient one? What response came from the decision role? These questions show whether the relevant repair occurred. They differ from asking everyone to rate Quinn’s integrity or asking Priya for a trust score.

A draft examination can supply further evidence: the group considers the sequence question and explains the resulting choice. It might retain the original option for a supported reason, choose another or identify missing information. Receiving a contribution does not guarantee its preferred result. An unchanged option does not automatically mean the repair was false; ask whether the relevant question was genuinely examined through the appropriate responsibility.

Now imagine another promised reading is missed. The earlier acknowledgment cannot prove the current arrangement works. Quinn should identify the new step, carry the available action and help examine the confirmation practice. Perhaps materials arrived after preparation closed, or a reading was claimed without checking. The actual account should determine the response; do not guess the cause or excuse failure because the earlier intention sounded sincere.

People may retain a cautious arrangement after good follow-through. The original trust model separates trust from its outcomes and keeps relationship and context specific. Delivered work can therefore be recognized without declaring a private feeling. Privately, consider whether you seek an immediate emotional sign of success instead of examining the commitment’s result. That insight needs no personnel assessment or real-case entry.

lessons.keyStatement: Evidence concerns what was carried through and what that supports; it cannot settle every private or wider outcome.

items.title: The reading happened
items.body: The example describes an actual reading and accurate summary. This is evidence of the promised action. Check that the question survived the summary; a tick beside read is not enough if its meaning changed. The work can be examined without a private confidence declaration.

items.title: Decision merits stay distinct
items.body: The responsible role clarifies draft status and arranges examination. A later selection concerns merits and evidence. Receiving a question is not a guarantee one option wins; retaining an option may be sound if the question was examined and the reason supported.

items.title: A new failure is new information
items.body: Another missed reading calls for response to that event and review of the usable practice. The earlier acknowledgment cannot cancel it. Examine actual dependencies or inaccurate confirmation instead of inventing a cause or treating sincerity as proof of delivery.

tabs.label: Intention proves delivery
tabs.body: Quinn says sincerity means everyone should accept the reading happened. This skips the action the promise concerned. Ask about the comparison and actual response; delivery evidence distinguishes an intention from work carried through without requiring an emotional judgment.

tabs.label: Only a preferred result counts
tabs.body: The group calls repair a failure unless Priya’s option wins. This confuses receiving a contribution with awarding a result. Examine the question’s consideration and supported reason while preserving actual selection responsibility.

tabs.label: The delivered action and open questions
tabs.body: The group names the reading, retained question and scoped decision response. Final selection and feelings remain open. This recognizes meaningful follow-through without making it proof of complete trust, universal benefit or an unexamined outcome.

check.question: What does the practice follow-through establish?
check.correct: The comparison was read, its question retained and a scoped response received; selection and private trust remain separate.
wrong: The earlier promise alone proves delivery.
Any outcome other than Priya’s preferred option proves the receiving failed.
A completed reading proves confidence in every later commitment.
check.feedbackCorrect: This accounts for delivered work without claiming the final merits or private relationship state.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A promise cannot prove delivery. Genuine examination can lead to a different supported choice. One reading cannot establish every private or future confidence state. Check the particular action and decision response, then state only what they support.

items.text: Quinn reads and preserves the actual question.
The responsible role clarifies draft status and arranges examination.
Which option will the proper process select?
How will the later commitment be carried through?
One reading proves every relationship is repaired.
The preferred option must win to be heard.

lessons.summary: Describe supported progress and unfinished responsibility without making the affected person validate the relationship or course.
lessons.objective: Describe mixed repair progress at the scope of the supplied evidence.
objectives: Describe mixed repair progress at the scope of the supplied evidence.
Identify an unfinished responsibility without erasing meaningful progress.
Choose a legitimate private or practical continuation without a trust declaration.
takeaways: Useful repair can coexist with open work and caution.
The affected person does not owe a success story.
Private learning and follow-through each matter without substituting for each other.
lessons.statement: Recognize supported progress and carry the responsibilities that remain.

image.caption: A credible repair connects a particular commitment with an action that can actually be carried through.

intro.heading: Progress without pressure to say everything is well
intro.body:
The combined cases now contain different states. Quinn read the comparison, retained the question and received draft-status clarification. Final selection remains unknown. Rowan corrected the explanation about Bea’s completed card without asking her to appear or reveal feelings. Bea called the factual correction useful, but did not declare every relationship concern resolved. Jo chose a clearer draft arrangement; her private confidence remains unknown.

These distinctions belong in an honest account. A useful correction is progress, an unfinished decision remains work, and a cautious arrangement is not proof the learning failed or complete trust returned. Do not flatten the account into everything repaired or nothing mattered. Its actual state helps identify a reasonable next responsibility.

Someone asks Bea for a moving story about how the apology transformed the gathering. Bea may decline. The correction concerned inaccurate information; her personal account is not owed to prove the learning’s value. A proportionate summary could describe the corrected explanation without reporting emotion. Actual information responsibilities still govern a later use of a story or work material.

The next step may be ordinary: complete examination through the responsible role, use the agreed question-and-response arrangement or carry a new commitment through. An actual formal concern continues with its assigned process. Consultant guidance can help staff examine difficulty, but staff retain their work and do not need a universal consultant sign-off to practice repair. A learning conversation cannot take over decision or investigation authority.

Privately, you may understand how you learned to recognize an apology, why caution feels uncomfortable or how a feasible small action differs from impressive reassurance. That insight matters without a report or work product. Optional practice can use a suitable situation without recording colleague feelings. This course cannot certify a restored relationship. Particular actions, context and freely chosen responses can support its continuing development over time.

lessons.keyStatement: An honest account can hold useful progress, open work and unknown private experience together.

items.title: Recognize the supplied useful correction
items.body: Bea called the factual correction useful. This supports a narrow positive account, not universal relationship improvement or forgiveness. Recognize the actual response without inflating it or treating the absence of a larger personal story as disappointing.

items.title: Leave unfinished work unfinished
items.body: Quinn’s reading and authority response are known; final selection is open. A cheerful summary cannot make the decision complete. The open decision also cannot erase the action performed. Choose the next responsibility from the actual state rather than an all-or-nothing account.

items.title: Allow private learning to remain private
items.body: Understanding a learned apology meaning or your reaction to caution need not produce a report. Fiction and silent reflection are complete routes. Optional practice concerns a suitable action and preserves duties, without collecting trust ratings or turning insight into personnel evidence.

tabs.label: Everything is repaired
tabs.body: The group declares all relationships and future promises restored because some actions occurred. This inflates a mixed record and can pressure people to agree. The unexamined private and future information remains unknown regardless of a cheerful statement.

tabs.label: Nothing matters without forgiveness
tabs.body: The group refuses to recognize a correction without Bea’s forgiveness declaration. Emotional certification becomes the condition for acknowledging delivered work. The correction can be useful while participants retain their own understanding of the relationship.

tabs.label: Progress with open work
tabs.body: The group names the reading, correction, useful supplied response and unfinished decision. It leaves Jo’s feelings unknown and offers private or suitable practice. This identifies next responsibilities without a universal result, success-story demand or employee assessment.

check.question: Which continuation is supported by the cases?
check.correct: Recognize the actions and useful supplied response, retain open responsibilities and allow private understanding or suitable practice without a trust declaration.
wrong: Require a public transformation story before Bea’s correction counts.
Declare every relationship repaired because Quinn completed reading.
Ignore delivered corrections because final selection and feelings remain unknown.
check.feedbackCorrect: This keeps progress and unfinished work distinct while respecting private understanding and personal choice.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A public emotional story is not owed to validate correction. One reading cannot establish all relationships. Unknown selection or feelings do not erase delivered work. Describe the mixed record and relevant next responsibility without a private certification test.

sorting.heading: Separate progress, open work and learning

items.text: Rowan corrected the explanation and Bea called it useful.
Quinn read and retained the question.
The final selection is not supplied.
Jo’s private confidence remains unknown.
Reflect silently on a learned acknowledgment meaning.
Use an example to practice a feasible repair.

lessons.next: You can revisit the cases or use the job aid privately. Specific acknowledgment, credible action and honest follow-through can support a relationship without requiring anyone to declare trust restored.

scenario.context: DSD practice case: The group reviews a completed reading, corrected explanation, Bea’s useful response, open selection and Jo’s chosen cautious arrangement. No universal relationship outcome was supplied.
scenario.prompt: Which closing account respects the learning?
options: Require private trust ratings before recognizing progress.
Say all future commitments are reliable because the course ended.
Describe the particular progress and open work while preserving private insight and suitable optional practice.
responses: This adds an emotional condition and personnel-style assessment.
Course completion cannot establish future delivery or everyone’s private experience.
This keeps the evidence honest and the next responsibility visible.

lessons.transfer: Choose silent reflection, complete an example or suitable optional practice. No confession, forgiveness account, trust rating or work result is required.

move.control: You can recognize repair while leaving private accounts and open decisions unclaimed.
move.failure: An emotional declaration or course completion certifies a whole relationship.
move.next: Name supported progress and a next responsibility, or retain an unrecorded private insight.

jobAid.subtitle: Name the setback, make a credible response and keep follow-through honest.
remember: Specific acknowledgment concerns the actual commitment and consequence rather than a required motive verdict.
Delivered work and private willingness to rely on it are different questions.
Repair does not require forgiveness, reassurance or a public success story.

sections.heading: Understand and acknowledge
items: Identify what was promised or claimed, what occurred and the supplied consequence.
Separate observed effect from private intention, feeling or a conclusion about a group.
Hear supplied learned meanings without making one public or private sequence universal.
Address an inaccurate public statement without requiring the person’s public emotion or presence.

sections.heading: Make the response credible
items: Choose an action you can deliver and name its responsible-role dependencies.
Do not promise another role’s selection or someone’s restored trust.
Make necessary work checkable through suitable ordinary material rather than collect trust ratings.
Offer personal repair dialogue as a choice, not a gate to work or actual concern response.
Managers and supervisors immediately report all allegations or incidents of protected-class harassment or discrimination to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures.

sections.heading: Follow through and continue
items: Check that the action happened and retained the actual question or meaning.
Keep receiving a contribution distinct from guaranteeing its preferred result.
Address a renewed failure as new information rather than rely on the earlier promise.
Recognize a supported correction and useful response while leaving open work and private feelings unknown.
Staff retain their work with consultant guidance available. Learning through private reflection matters without a report or work result.

sources.title: Mayer, Davis and Schoorman: An integrative model of organizational trust
sources.note: The 1995 conceptual article separates trust, contributing perceptions and outcomes within an organizational relationship. These distinctions inform the commitment examples; they do not rate employees or guarantee that an apology restores trust.

sources.title: Council of Europe: Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Original discussion of individual learned meanings, comparison and adaptation without compulsory imitation supports the newly authored Bea/Rowan encounter. It is not a national-style list or individual assessment.

sources.title: DHS Equity Policy
sources.note: Actual staff work and equity-analysis responsibilities remain separate from voluntary repair practice. The course changes no approval authority and creates no universal consultant gate.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1432: Respectful workplace
sources.note: Actual respectful-workplace scope and response roles remain applicable. Ordinary disagreement or a missed draft step is not automatically a formal finding; optional reconciliation does not replace an available formal process.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1436: Harassment and discrimination prohibited
sources.note: Managers and supervisors immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures. Relationship repair cannot delay reporting or substitute for assigned investigation.
